guide.summary: Parks, a free ferry, the tram, observation decks and museums, with breakfast spots, dinners, cocktail bars, bakeries and coffee checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Plan museum days around Tuesdays, when the Whitney and the Frick are both closed, and book the Empire State Building ahead because every visit needs a timed reservation.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: The Whitney Museum of American Art and The Frick Collection are both closed on Tuesdays. The 9/11 Museum opens Wednesday to Monday with select Tuesdays, while the Memorial is open daily 8 a.m.-8 p.m.

toolkit.label: Timed tickets
toolkit.copy: All Empire State Building visits require a timed reservation, with 86th-floor tickets from $46, and the 9/11 Museum requires advance ticket purchase. The Frick recommends timed tickets, and last tickets are sold one hour before closing.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins and tables
toolkit.copy: Russ & Daughters Cafe takes no reservations, and Via Carota says walk-ins are always welcome. L'Artusi releases Resy tables two weeks ahead at 9 AM, and at Employees Only cocktails are walk-in only while the dining room needs a dinner reservation.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Attaboy is 21+, needs a valid physical government-issued ID and takes parties of six and under. The Frick admits only children aged 10 and older, and Bemelmans Bar discourages athletic and casual leisure wear.

guide.dek: Spend your mornings at the parks and museums, book timed tickets and dinner tables ahead, and leave the walk-in cafés and bars for when you have time to wait.
intro: Start outdoors. According to the Central Park Conservancy, Central Park opens at 6:00 am and closes at 1:00 am, 365 days a year. The Central Park Zoo entrance is at 64th Street and 5th Avenue, and the zoo is open 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM on weekdays through October 31, 2026, then 10:00 AM to 4:30 PM daily from November 1. The High Line is open 7am to 10pm until November 30, then 7am to 8pm. Its site posted a temporary closure of the stretch between 18th and 23rd Streets on October 19.

For harbor and skyline views, the Staten Island Ferry is free and runs around the clock from Whitehall Terminal at 4 South Street. The City warns you about scammers selling fake tickets. The 9/11 Memorial at 180 Greenwich Street is free and open daily 8 a.m.-8 p.m. The Museum requires advance tickets and is open Wednesday to Monday. Every Empire State Building visit needs a timed reservation, with 86th-floor tickets from $46. The Roosevelt Island Tram leaves from East 60th Street and Second Avenue and takes standard MTA fares, including OMNY.

Tuesday is the closing day at both the Whitney Museum of American Art on Gansevoort Street and The Frick Collection at 1 East 70th Street. The Whitney stays open until 10 pm on Fridays, with Free Friday Nights from 5 to 10 pm, and its current shows include Roy Lichtenstein: Like New. The Frick recommends timed tickets, admits only children aged 10 and older, and has Pay-What-You-Wish admission on Wednesdays from 1:30 to 5:30 p.m. At Chelsea Market, 75 9th Ave, the concourse is open 7 am to 10 pm, and trick-or-treating is scheduled for October 31, 2026.

For food, Russ & Daughters Cafe at 127 Orchard Street is walk-in only with no takeout. Via Carota on Grove Street welcomes walk-ins, and L'Artusi releases Resy tables two weeks ahead at 9 AM, keeping bar and counter seats for walk-ins. Katz's Delicatessen at 205 East Houston Street opens at 8:00 AM. For drinks, Attaboy on Eldridge Street is 21+, takes parties of six and under, and asks for a physical ID. Bemelmans Bar at The Carlyle has pianists from 5:30 pm and a jazz trio from 9 pm, with a cover charge that depends on the artist.
summaryCards: Pair a free Staten Island Ferry ride with the 9/11 Memorial and a timed Empire State Building slot, then walk Central Park, which is open 6:00 am to 1:00 am.
Take a walk-in table at Russ & Daughters Cafe from 8:30 AM, then pick up coffee at Stumptown on West 8th Street before the High Line opens its gates at 7am.
Check that your museum day isn't a Tuesday, book L'Artusi on Resy when tables release at 9 AM two weeks out, and bring physical ID if you plan to go to Attaboy.

limitations: This is a website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several official sites could not be read by automated fetch and were left out rather than bypassed: Top of the Rock, the American Museum of Natural History, MoMA and Grand Central Terminal (HTTP 403), The Met and the Brooklyn Museum (HTTP 429), the Guggenheim (cookie wall only), the NYPL main branch (empty page), Bubby's (connection refused), Mah-Ze-Dahr (HTTP 404) and NYC Parks' Central Park page (HTTP 403; the Conservancy site was used instead). Some places were only partly published. Crown Shy, Attaboy and Devoción showed hours but no dated content. The Whitney listed exhibitions without dates. The Frick page carried one apparently stale notice. Employees Only's reservations page may be out of date. Katz's listed weekly hours that conflict with its "open 24 hrs on weekends" banner. The High Line's closure notice and Central Park's event dates had no year shown.
